# Theoretical Motivation

---

## Executive Overview

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### The Challenge
* College football has high schedule asymmetry across 134 FBS & 128 FCS teams.
* Media polls (AP / Coaches) suffer from recency bias, pre-season inertia, and margin-of-victory confounding.
* Predictive models (SP+, FPI) forecast *hypothetical* spreads, not *earned accomplishment*.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Our Bayesian Solution
* **Retrospective Evaluation:** What did teams earn given final opponent strength?
* **4-Pipeline Architecture:** 2×2 orthogonal matrix (Actual vs. Expected × Discrete vs. Continuous).
* **Sparse Graph Regularization:** Non-centered hierarchical shrinkage for FCS connections.
:::
:::

---

## The 2×2 Performance Matrix

| Granularity \ Domain | **Actual (Scoreboard Realized)** | **Expected (Play EPA Dominance)** |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Discrete (Game Resumes)** | **Pipeline 1: WLD ($\theta$)**<br>Ordered Logit $\{L, OTL, OTW, W\}$ | **Pipeline 3: XWLD ($\omega$)**<br>Ordered Logit on Post-Game Win Expectancy |
| **Continuous (Margins)** | **Pipeline 2: PD ($\delta$)**<br>Robust Student-$t$ on Point Differential | **Pipeline 4: XPD ($\alpha$)**<br>Robust Student-$t$ on Net Play EPA |

$$\text{Composite Index} = w_{\text{wld}} \Phi(Z_\theta) + w_{\text{pd}} \Phi(Z_\delta) + w_{\text{xwld}} \Phi(Z_\omega) + w_{\text{xpd}} \Phi(Z_\alpha)$$

---

## Graph Disconnection & The FCS Silo

* CFB competition forms a **directed multi-graph** $\mathcal{G} = (\mathcal{V}, \mathcal{E})$.
* Across 134 FBS teams and 128 FCS teams:
  * Only ~110 cross-division matchups occur annually.
  * Connectivity is sparse and one-sided (FBS hosts ~98% of matchups).
* **Failure of flat priors:**
  * Top FCS teams can inflate via internal transitive cycles without proper regularization.
* **Our Solution:** Hierarchical Bayesian shrinkage.

---

# The 4-Pipeline Performance Matrix

---

## Pipeline 1: WLD Ordered Logit (Actual Discrete)

We map discrete game outcomes $Y_k \in \{1: \text{L}, 2: \text{OTL}, 3: \text{OTW}, 4: \text{W}\}$:

$$Y_k \sim \text{OrderedLogit}(\eta_k^{\text{wld}}, \mathbf{c}_{\text{wld}})$$

$$\eta_k^{\text{wld}} = \theta_{\text{home}[k]} - \theta_{\text{away}[k]} + \gamma_{\text{home}} \cdot (1 - \text{neutral}_k)$$

* $\theta_i$: Latent actual resume strength of team $i$.
* $\gamma_{\text{home}} \sim \mathcal{N}(0.2, 0.1^2)$: Home field advantage log-odds.
* $\mathbf{c}_{\text{wld}} = (c_1, c_2, c_3)$: Ordered cutpoint thresholds.

---

## Pipeline 2: PD Robust Student-$t$ (Actual Margin)

Raw scoreboard point differential $\Delta \text{Pts}_k = \text{Score}_{\text{home}} - \text{Score}_{\text{away}}$:

$$\Delta \text{Pts}_k \sim \text{Student-}t\left(\nu_{\text{pd}}, \, \delta_{\text{home}[k]} - \delta_{\text{away}[k]} + \beta_{\text{home, pd}} \cdot (1 - \text{neutral}_k), \, \tau_{\text{pd}}^2\right)$$

* $\delta_i$: Latent actual point differential rating.
* $\nu_{\text{pd}} \sim \text{Gamma}(2, 0.1)$: Heavy-tailed degree of freedom protects against extreme blowout leverage.
* $\beta_{\text{home, pd}} \sim \mathcal{N}(2.8, 1.0)$: Home field advantage in points.

---

## Pipeline 3: XWLD Ordered Logit (Expected Discrete)

Post-Game Win Expectancy (PGWE) mapped to expected discrete categories $Y^{\text{exp}}_k \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$:

$$Y^{\text{exp}}_k \sim \text{OrderedLogit}(\eta_k^{\text{xwld}}, \mathbf{c}_{\text{xwld}})$$

$$\eta_k^{\text{xwld}} = \omega_{\text{home}[k]} - \omega_{\text{away}[k]} + \gamma_{\text{home, xwld}} \cdot (1 - \text{neutral}_k)$$

* $\omega_i$: Latent expected outcome ability (deserved wins).
* **$\theta_i - \omega_i$:** Direct mathematical measure of **Resume Luck**.

---

## Pipeline 4: XPD Student-$t$ (Expected Margin)

Net Expected Points Added (EPA) aggregated across all offensive plays:

$$\text{XPD}_k = \sum_{p \in \text{Plays}(k)} \text{EPA}_{p, \text{home}} - \sum_{p \in \text{Plays}(k)} \text{EPA}_{p, \text{away}}$$

$$\text{XPD}_k \sim \text{Student-}t\left(\nu_{\text{xpd}}, \, \alpha_{\text{home}[k]} - \alpha_{\text{away}[k]} + \beta_{\text{home, xpd}} \cdot (1 - \text{neutral}_k), \, \tau_{\text{xpd}}^2\right)$$

* $\alpha_i$: Latent per-play efficiency rating.
* **$\delta_i - \alpha_i$:** Direct measure of **Finishing / Red-Zone Margin Luck**.

---

# Sparse Graph Shrinkage & Schedule Equity

---

## Hierarchical FCS Regularization

To connect the sparse graph without arbitrary penalty downweighting:

$$\theta_i \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\mu_{\text{sub}[i]}, \, \sigma^2_{\text{sub}[i]}\right)$$

$$\mu_{\text{FBS}} = 0 \quad (\text{Identifiability Anchor})$$

$$\mu_{\text{FCS}} \sim \mathcal{N}(-1.5, 0.5^2) \quad [\text{or } \xi_{\text{FCS, pd}} \sim \mathcal{N}(-24.0, 4.0^2) \text{ in PD}]$$

* **Elite FCS Programs:** (e.g. North Dakota State) shrink toward upper tail of $\mathcal{N}(\mu_{\text{FCS}}, \sigma^2_{\text{FCS}})$.
* **Weak FCS Programs:** Yield negligible resume equity in $\theta$ and cap point differential gains.

---

## Sonneborn-Berger & Buchholz Metrics

Map posterior opponent strength into game equity: $\mathcal{M}(\theta_j) = \text{logit}^{-1}(\theta_j)$

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Sonneborn-Berger (SB)
$$\text{SB}_i = \sum_{k \in \text{Games}(i)} w_{k, i} \cdot \mathcal{M}(\theta_{\text{opp}[k]})$$
* Outcome weight $w_{k, i} \in \{0, 1, 2, 3\}$.
* Directly rewards defeating high-quality opponents.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Buchholz (BH / SOS)
$$\text{BH}_i = \sum_{k \in \text{Games}(i)} \mathcal{M}(\theta_{\text{opp}[k]})$$
* Sum of total schedule difficulty faced.
:::
:::

---

## High-Dimensional Bradley-Terry Insights

Recent theoretical advances formalize non-asymptotic behavior on sparse graphs:

> **Fang, Han, Luo, & Xu (2026)**, *Recent advances in the Bradley–Terry Model: theory, algorithms, and applications*, arXiv:2601.14727.

* Establishes convergence rates under irregular comparison topologies ($p \ll n$).
* Verifies that hierarchical Gaussian shrinkage enforces spectral gap stability.
* Confirms uniform consistency over dynamic ranges when anchor sets are identifiability-constrained.

# Computational Architecture & Quality Control

---

## Production Pipeline: `targets` + DuckDB

```
[ cfbfastR / CFBD API ]
          │
          ▼
   [ data/cfb.duckdb ]  ◄── Incremental Sync (Weekly)
          │
    targets Graph
    ├── 1. raw_schedules_pbp
    ├── 2. transform_all_pipelines (WLD, PD, XWLD, XPD)
    ├── 3. fit_wld_stan (cmdstanr)
    ├── 4. fit_pd_stan (cmdstanr)
    ├── 5. fit_xwld_stan (cmdstanr)
    ├── 6. fit_xpd_stan (cmdstanr)
    ├── 7. convergence_diagnostics (R-hat <= 1.01, ESS >= 400)
    ├── 8. prior_sensitivity_sweep (Spearman rho >= 0.985)
    ├── 9. 4-way composite_rankings & benchmark comparison
    └── 10. render_reports_and_dashboards
```

---

## Diagnostic Gates & Quality Control

Target pipeline halts if MCMC convergence fails across any pipeline:

| Diagnostic Metric | Strict Threshold | Justification |
|:---|:---:|:---|
| **Max $\widehat{R}$** | $\le 1.01$ | Chains have thoroughly mixed |
| **Min $\text{ESS}_{\text{bulk}}$** | $\ge 400$ | Stable posterior mean & median |
| **Min $\text{ESS}_{\text{tail}}$** | $\ge 400$ | Accurate tail credible intervals |
| **Post-warmup Divergences** | $= 0$ | No geometric funnel traps |
| **Prior Sensitivity $\rho$** | $\ge 0.985$ | Robust to FCS hyperparameter shift |

---

## Conclusion

* 4-pipeline architecture completes the **2×2 performance decomposition** (Actual vs. Expected × Discrete vs. Continuous).
* Cross-pipeline deltas directly compute **Resume Luck** ($\theta - \omega$) and **Finishing Luck** ($\delta - \alpha$).
* Non-centered hierarchical modeling enables robust estimation across 260+ teams.
* Complete reproducibility managed by `targets` and DuckDB.

**Thank you!**
